_about: Gap-first eval scenarios for the Requirements Agent. Each scenario is anchored to a real failure mode the bare model exhibits without the skill. Expected behavior is split into deterministic assertions and semantic review by /evaluate-run's quality reviewer or a human. Paths in deterministic checks are relative to the run's outputs directory.

scenarios.name: input-eval-surfaces-gaps-and-contradiction
scenarios.gap: Without the skill, the model jumps straight to drafting and never records that retention is contradictory (5y vs 7y) or that 'fast' is unquantified.
scenarios.prompt: Start a run for this corpus and generate BRD and FRD.
expected_behavior: Updates input_evaluation.md and state.json; selects BRD and FRD only
Records the 5-year vs 7-year retention contradiction as an open question / gap
Flags 'should be fast' as an unquantified requirement
Detects a PII/compliance signal from the masked contact fields
Does NOT auto-advance into extraction
qualitative_review: Retention contradiction is surfaced, not silently resolved
'fast' is called out as needing a measurable target

scenarios.name: no-fabricated-kpi-target
scenarios.gap: The bare model invents a plausible on-time-delivery target (e.g. 95%) that no source states.
scenarios.prompt: Extract the analysis layer for this run.
expected_behavior: Linked topic pages include the on-time-delivery KPI (KPI-*) with no invented numeric target and an [INSUFFICIENT INPUT] marker
The linked knowledge graph records the retention conflict
A linked topic page preserves client ID REQ-014 and its source evidence
qualitative_review: On-time-delivery KPI carries no fabricated target value
REQ-014 is preserved as a client-canonical source ID

scenarios.name: happy-path-ids-and-lint-clean
scenarios.gap: Bare model produces a generic BRD with no stable IDs, no KBQ/KPI sections, and leaked template residue.
scenarios.prompt: Generate the BRD for this run.
expected_behavior: Writes BRD.md embedding use cases, KBQs, KPIs/metrics, business rules
Every business requirement carries a stable ID
No leaked template comments or placeholders
Ends the turn with a recommendation; does not auto-run the FRD
qualitative_review: Executive summary is specific to order analytics, not boilerplate

scenarios.name: no-hallucinated-kpi-target-and-vague-not-laundered
scenarios.gap: Bare model launders 'should be fast' into a requirement verbatim and invents an on-time-delivery target.
scenarios.prompt: Generate the BRD for this run.
expected_behavior: On-time-delivery KPI appears without an invented target — marked [INSUFFICIENT INPUT] with an Open Item
'fast' is not stated as a formal requirement; it is made measurable or flagged
Every inline marker has a matching Open Items row
qualitative_review: No numeric KPI target appears that is not sourced
Vague 'fast' phrasing is not copied into a 'shall' requirement

scenarios.name: data-requirements-and-failure-handling
scenarios.gap: Bare model omits the masking constraint and the missing-feed failure path.
scenarios.prompt: Generate the FRD for this run.
expected_behavior: Data requirements map orders_feed -> fact_orders at entity level
PII masking appears as a constraint/NFR before warehouse write
A failure-handling FR covers missing/malformed feed (retain partition + alert)
Every functional/NFR statement is testable
qualitative_review: Failure path (missing feed -> keep prior data + alert) is captured as a requirement

scenarios.name: user-centered-verifiable-atomic
scenarios.gap: Bare model writes implementation-level, compound URS rows with no verification method.
scenarios.prompt: Generate the URS for this run.
expected_behavior: Each URS row has a verification method from the enumerated set
No compound (multi-shall) requirements
PII/retention rows carry a criticality value
qualitative_review: Requirements are user-outcome level, not solution design
Verification methods are appropriate to criticality

scenarios.name: vertical-slice-and-persona-discipline
scenarios.gap: Bare model decomposes by pipeline stage (trigger/DQ/load) and uses 'the pipeline' or a business stakeholder as the story persona.
scenarios.prompt: Generate the Jira story pack for this run.
expected_behavior: Stories are vertical slices (entity/outcome), never per pipeline stage
Each story persona is a delivery-team role (BA/Developer/Tester/Reviewer), not a system or business stakeholder
Each story has acceptance criteria and cites REQ-014 where relevant
Size/Estimate stays TBD (no invented story points)
qualitative_review: No story titled after a pipeline stage/step/layer
Persona slot is always a team role; business stakeholders appear in the benefit clause

scenarios.name: cascade-propagation-and-id-preservation
scenarios.gap: Bare model edits only the file the user named and leaves derived artifacts inconsistent.
scenarios.prompt: Set the on-time-delivery KPI target to 95% (after BRD and FRD already exist).
expected_behavior: Updates the linked KPI topic and the BRD block that owns it
Marks only dependent FRD/story blocks dirty and applies targeted changes
Refreshes final traceability from linked pages while preserving all stable IDs
Does not renumber surviving IDs; deleted entities are removed from owned blocks
qualitative_review: Every artifact referencing the KPI value is updated to 95% after approval
Stable IDs are preserved across the revision
